chunks: A pregnant woman came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful! I have committed adultery — purify me, may God purify you, for the punishment of this world is easier than the unending punishment of the Hereafter.' He said to her: 'From what shall I purify you?' She said: 'I have committed adultery.' He said to her: 'Are you a married woman or otherwise?' She said: 'Rather, I am married.' He said: 'Was your husband present when you did what you did, or was he absent from you?' She said: 'Rather, he was present.' He said to her: 'Go and give birth to what is in your womb, then come to me and I will purify you.' When the woman had turned away from him and reached a place where she could not hear his words, he said: 'O God, this is one testimony.' Shortly thereafter she came to him and said: 'I have given birth — purify me.' He feigned ignorance and said: 'Purify you, O servant of God? From what?' She said: 'I committed adultery — purify me.' He said: 'And you were a married woman when you did what you did?' She said: 'Yes.' He said: 'And was your husband present or absent?' She said: 'Rather, he was present.' He said: 'Go and breastfeed him for two complete years as God commanded you.' The woman departed, and when she reached where she could not hear his words, he said: 'O God, this is two testimonies.' When two years had passed, the woman came and said: 'I have breastfed him for two years — purify me, O Commander of the Faithful.' He feigned ignorance and said: 'Purify you from what?' She said: 'I committed adultery — purify me.' He said: 'And you were a married woman when you did what you did?' She said: 'Yes.' He said: 'And was your husband absent from you when you did what you did, or was he present?' She said: 'Rather, he was present.' He said: 'Go and provide for him until he is old enough to eat, drink, not fall from a rooftop, and not tumble into a well.' She departed weeping. When she turned away and reached where she could not hear his words, he said: 'O God, this is three testimonies.'

Amr ibn Hurayth al-Makhzumi met her and said: 'Why are you weeping, O servant of God? I have seen you coming repeatedly to Ali asking him to purify you.' She said: 'I came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and asked him to purify me, and he said: Provide for your child until he can eat, drink, not fall from a rooftop, and not tumble into a well — and I fear that death will come upon me before he purifies me.' Amr ibn Hurayth said to her: 'Return to him, for I will provide for the child.' She returned and informed the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) of what Amr had said. The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to her, feigning ignorance: 'Why should Amr provide for your child?' She said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, I have committed adultery — purify me.' He said: 'And you were a married woman when you did what you did?' She said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Was your husband absent from you when you did what you did, or present?' She said: 'Rather, he was present.' He raised his head toward the sky and said: 'O God, four testimonies have now been established against her before You, and You have told Your Prophet (may God’s blessings be upon him and his family) in what You informed him of Your religion: O Muhammad, whoever suspends one of My prescribed limits has opposed Me and sought thereby to contradict Me. O God, I am not suspending Your limits, nor seeking to contradict You, nor neglecting Your rulings — rather I am obedient to You and following the sunnah of Your Prophet (may God’s blessings be upon him and his family).' Amr ibn Hurayth looked at him as though pomegranate seeds were bursting across his face. When Amr saw that, he said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, I only meant to provide for the child when I thought you would want that; but if you dislike it, I will not do it.' The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'After four testimonies by God, you shall provide for him — and you shall do so in a state of humiliation.'

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) then ascended the pulpit and said: 'O Qanbar, call the people to a congregational prayer.' Qanbar called out to the people and they gathered until the mosque was packed. The Commander of the Faithful (blessings of God upon him) stood, praised God and extolled Him, then said: 'O people, your Imam is going forth with this woman to this open plain to establish upon her the hadd, God willing. The Commander of the Faithful commands you: go out disguised, with your stones, no one recognizing another, until you return to your homes, God willing.' He then descended. When morning came, he went forth with the woman, and the people went out disguised, faces wrapped in their turbans and cloaks, stones in their cloaks and sleeves, until he arrived at the open plain of Kufa with the people alongside him. He ordered that a pit be dug for her; then he buried her in it. Then he mounted his mule, planted his feet firmly in the stirrups, placed his two index fingers in his ears, and called out at the top of his voice: 'O people, God Blessed and Exalted made a covenant with His Prophet (may God’s blessings be upon him and his family) — a covenant that Muhammad (may God’s blessings be upon him and his family) transmitted to me — that one who himself owes God a hadd shall not administer the hadd. Whoever has upon him a hadd like what she has, let him not administer the hadd upon her.' All the people departed that day, except the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (peace be upon them). These three alone administered the hadd upon her that day, and there was no one with them but themselves. And he departed.

[A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), said: A pregnant woman came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: 'I have done it — purify me.' Then he mentioned a similar account.]

key_terms.الزِّنَا: Zinna (adultery/fornication) — one of the hadd offences
key_terms.الشَّهَادَةُ: Testimony/confession — here referring to the woman's voluntary declarations
key_terms.الطَّهَارَةُ: Purification — used by the woman as a euphemism for receiving the hadd penalty as expiation
key_terms.الظَّهْر: Open plain/outskirts — the area outside Kufa where the execution was carried out
key_terms.الْحَدُّ: Hadd — the prescribed, fixed legal punishment in Islamic law for certain offences
key_terms.صَاغِرٌ: Humiliated/abased — the state in which Amr was required to comply
key_terms.مُتَنَكِّرُونَ: Disguised — the Imam instructed the people to conceal their identities
key_terms.مُجِحٌّ: A woman in the final stage of pregnancy, about to give birth

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali handle a pregnant woman's confession of adultery in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This legal case narrative describes Imam Ali's (AS) meticulous, compassionate judicial procedure for handling a married woman's repeated confession of adultery. The Imam employed a remarkable legal strategy: each time the woman came to confess, he feigned ignorance to require her to make a fresh, voluntary declaration, while simultaneously finding grounds to delay executing the hadd penalty — first waiting for her to give birth, then to complete breastfeeding, then to raise the child to self-sufficiency. In the background, he privately acknowledged each new testimony to God. When Amr ibn Hurayth al-Makhzumi offered to relieve the woman of the childcare obligation (inadvertently helping her reach the required four testimonies faster), the Imam then publicly proclaimed — before a full congregation in Kufa — that no one who himself owes God a hadd should participate in carrying out a hadd. When all others withdrew, only the Imam, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (AS) administered the punishment. The narrative illustrates Shia jurisprudential principles regarding: the four-testimony threshold for zinna cases, the Imam's discretion in managing confessions, protection of the child's rights, and the moral integrity required of those who execute legal punishments. The concluding brief hadith from Abu Abdillah (AS) confirms a similar account, reinforcing the precedent.
